video.title: AI Builds the Websites That Pay You Monthly

summary: Chris Koerner demonstrates how to build local service lead-generation websites with Hostinger Horizons, then sell the leads to businesses in the area. He recommends choosing a growing niche and market, using a location-and-service domain, and improving the site with local SEO. His suggested sales approach is to wait for real leads, give an initial batch to a business for free, and then offer exclusivity. He also discusses website sales and advertising as other ways to monetize websites, while noting that some sites may never generate leads.

acquisition.how: Agents can help build pages and draft local SEO content, but ranking takes time and the speaker recommends human work on backlinks and local business listings. Contacting a lead buyer also needs a lawful, effective process.

onboarding.how: A system could record lead buyers and share evidence of lead quality, but the speaker's approach depends on a human finding and persuading a local business, then agreeing exclusivity.

delivery.how: Forms, call tracking and lead forwarding could be automated with routine human checks. The transcript does not explain call handling, lead validation or dispute resolution.

billing.how: The speaker demonstrates an AI-generated invoice portal connected to Stripe. Invoices and payments could run with occasional human review.

support.how: Agents could answer routine buyer questions, but lead-quality disputes and exclusivity or service issues would likely need a human.

uk_applicability.notes: Local search and selling service leads can work in the UK. Use UK market and location research, and handle personal data and lead sharing in line with UK requirements. The transcript demonstrates US cities and .com domains, so local choices would need adapting.

risks: The speaker says some sites will not generate many leads, so building several sites may produce uneven results.
SEO rankings and lead flow may take weeks or months; a site being built does not establish that it will rank.
A buyer may reject leads or dispute their quality; the transcript does not explain qualification, refunds or dispute terms.

In the UK, lead collection and sharing need appropriate data protection practices. Unsolicited electronic marketing to individuals and sole traders is restricted by PECR; buyer outreach needs a lawful channel.

tactics.name: Choose a service and market using search and growth signals
steps: Use Google Trends to check whether searches for the service, such as pool service near me, are trending upward in the target country.
Check whether the service has a demand pattern that fits the business; the speaker treats seasonality as acceptable.
Choose a growing city and check whether local demand appears plausible before building the site.

quote.text: But before we build the website, we gotta know what website to build, what niche are we building in, and what markets are we building in?
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Use a service-and-city domain and repeatable site template
steps: Choose a domain combining the service and city, such as the pool-service example in the transcript.
Use an AI site builder to make a clean, mobile-first local lead-generation site with service, area, contact and SEO content.
Give the AI the business intent and explain that the site will be adapted for other locations and niches.
Reuse the structure for another service and market, then review the generated content before publishing.

quote.text: It's important to tell any AI what your intent is, right? Give it context and tell it your intent because it's going to know more about what you're wanting than what you even know because we've never done this before, right?
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Reduce lead-form friction according to service value
steps: For a low-ticket service, test a short form to reduce barriers to submission.
For a higher-ticket service, add questions that qualify the prospect, such as project size and property details.
Compare lead volume with close rate rather than optimizing only for the number of form submissions.
Treat the right balance of form friction and prospect intent as specific to the niche.

quote.text: There is a perfect trade-off between friction and intent, okay, and conversion rate. Don't ever forget that. The trick is to find the balance for you and your niche.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Publish, connect the domain and set up payment infrastructure
steps: Publish the generated site on its temporary domain to review it.
Register or connect the chosen custom domain and publish the site again.
If buyers will pay through the site, ask the builder to create an invoice area and connect Stripe using an API key.
Keep the API key private; the speaker says he blurred it out in the demonstration.

quote.text: Boom, just like that, I didn't even ask for it, but now I have an admin portal, where I can send invoices, see invoices, and others can come and pay invoices, all because I just gave it my one Stripe API key, awesome.

tactics.name: Add local SEO foundations and links
steps: Include local keywords, meta tags, meta descriptions, headings and location-relevant content.
Add blog articles and mention nearby cities where appropriate.
Create a Google Business Profile.

steps: Wait until the site produces leads before approaching a local service business.
Offer the first leads for free so the business can verify that they are real and useful.
After demonstrating lead quality, offer ongoing or exclusive access to the leads.
Use exclusivity to support a higher price, while confirming the buyer's terms directly.

quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: A repeatable template can make it easier to test another service or location, but each site's results can differ.

quote.text: Not all of them will have fish, but the more hooks we set out, AKA the more websites we build, the more money we'll make.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Local businesses may underinvest in internet marketing even when their existing website still produces leads, creating room for a marketer to improve it.

quote.text: Their website was built in 2009. It still generates leads for them, but they don't know how much better it could be if they actually optimized it.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Treat optional monetization methods as strategic choices. Ads may add revenue, but the speaker chooses to focus on selling leads for this site.

quote.text: I don't wanna do that here, but it's not a bad idea, 'cause you're not really gonna turn customers away if your site has ads on it
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Use a customer-facing process that makes payment and invoicing easier; the speaker demonstrates generating an invoice portal through the site builder.

quote.text: now I have an admin portal, where I can send invoices, see invoices, and others can come and pay invoices
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

evidence_quality.rationale: This is a host-led tutorial with a live website-builder demonstration and some first-hand examples, but the central revenue figures are either attributed to an unnamed operator or presented as hypothetical. The transcript does not demonstrate actual rankings, lead sales or revenue from the showcased site. Several captions appear misheard, including the claimed monthly revenue amount.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Chris Koerner promotes Hostinger Horizons, directs viewers to his link, gives a promo code for a discount, and says Hostinger supports his site.
